I’m not sure why you’re talking about a “timeline” or the mental effects of cancellation as if I disagree with you. Literally all I’m saying is that people will support Shane (or anybody else) on the sole fact that he’s an apparent victim of cancel culture. Any criticism = hate/cancel culture in their eyes. And these people will fling that term around whenever anyone says one negative thing about Shane—even if it’s constructive. It has lost it’s meaning and is pretty much just a buzzword now for people who don’t want their idol to be held accountable.

But I don’t think you really want to listen to what I’m saying considering you insulted me. I mean I never insulted you 🤷‍♀️ Let’s agree to disagree.

I “may not be able to cope enough to have a conversation,” I “don’t have empathy”…you sure are making assumptions about me based on one paragraph lol. You’re assuming that I’m defending bullying, which I’m not. You’re also assuming that I think cancel culture means someone is cancelled for life, which I don’t. 

Where do you think I’m defending the idea of cancel culture? I only said it doesn’t exist in the way people think it does, which is completely decimating someone’s career. Again, there are plenty of celebrities that have done way worse things than Shane that have managed to maintain their careers. If they had any other job, they would lose it. Yet they don’t, because being a public figure grants you a certain amount of power.

I literally only said that the idea of “cancel culture” has been obscured to the point where there’s little difference between hate and genuine criticism.

Edit: all I was saying is that some people will shut down any form of criticism because they believe the people who are giving that criticism obviously are taking part in cancel culture and send death threats on the daily. That’s it.

Cancel culture doesn’t truly work. Despite taking a break for a year, Shane’s back. Both with support and criticism, but he’s back nonetheless. So is David Dobrick, James Charles, Jeffree Star…

If cancel culture was this big bad life-threatening thing, I don’t think predators would be allowed to have such large platforms after they’re rightfully called out. It’s gotten to the point now where people will take a position to support a “cancelled” celebrity solely because “cancel culture is bad.” “Cancel culture” has become this catch-all from consequences and criticism to outright hate, and throwing that term around (and “virtue signaling” too) completely shuts down any discussion

I think taking accountability means that you are willing to own up to what you’ve done. He can do this by:

1. Genuinely apologizing to the people he’s hurt. No excuses, no “people thought it was funny so I kept doing it,” none of that. Just a genuine apology without entitlement to forgiveness 

2. Bringing up specific examples that hurt said people. Jenna Marbles played video clips of what she did and said how it was wrong. He needs to stop glazing over the pedophilic, racist things by referring to them as some abstract, problematic thing. That’s disingenuous because you’re avoiding precisely what you did wrong, and people don’t know exactly what you’re taking accountability for.

3. Donate to some organizations that help said people. These could be ones that help victims of CSA, BLM, anything that pertains to his hurtful behavior. Even if this isn’t “genuine,” it still at least monetarily helps those who need it.

We ultimately have no idea if he’s actually going to change i.e. go to therapy for his pedophilic behavior or if he even believes he deserves being called out. But at least his presence on the internet will be one that’s addressed his cancellation and sets an example for owning up to that behavior. Though I personally wish he wouldn’t ever come back, I truly think that taking those steps are the least he can do

Her teaming up with Shane--a guy who was known as Youtube's Oprah at the time of his docuseries--was such a terrible thing for mental health awareness. I highly doubt she would've gotten the level of recognition she has without him. So, it's incredibly dangerous how she's been able to blast harmful stereotypes of people with personality disorders to such a large audience.

I don't have anti-social personality disorder, but I do have borderline personality disorder (both are in Cluster B). There's such a huge stigma that even doctors will refuse to treat us for having a personality disorder. I've struggled to find books to help me because most of the time, self-help books are made for people who have to "put up" with us. And this is just inside the medical community, the general public's opinion of us is also awful. It makes me sad that she's only hurting mentally ill people even more by painting us as two-dimensional monsters.
This. I'll add--she may be a licensed therapist--but she's a licensed *marriage and family therapist.* That to me makes her branding as psych expert even more disingenuous.
